AI and the assistant

  • Enable only what you want
  • Choose Low, Medium or High
  • Ask for facts or instructions
  • Search before acting
  • Ranking, matching and privacy
  • Connect an external assistant with MCP
  • When the assistant cannot help

Set up AI, choose a model tier, ask for help and connect an external assistant securely.

Enable only what you want

AI is off by default. An administrator needs an account with an AI provider, or a running local model service, before enabling it. A provider is the service that runs the model and receives your AI requests.

  1. Open Configuration → AI and enable AI.
  2. Choose your provider. Enter its API key if required. For a custom service, enter its base URL and check that it supports the OpenAI-compatible API, the request format Arrk uses. A local service must be reachable from Arrk, not just from your browser.
  3. Enter a Medium model supported by your provider. Choose Low and High models if you want different options for cost and capability.
  4. Review the individual feature switches. Enable the assistant for chat; review automatic features before allowing background usage.
  5. Open AI Usage at /ai and select Test AI. Read the result before trying the assistant.

Test AI makes a real request with your Medium model and saved settings. A successful test does not guarantee every model or feature works; try your intended task too. If it fails, check the provider, exact model name, endpoint, key and account limits.

For manual setup, the main keys are ai.enabled, ai.provider, ai.apiKey, ai.baseUrl and ai.models.medium.

Choose Low, Medium or High

Use Model tier in the assistant to choose the trade-off for a question. All tiers use the configured provider.

  • Low is intended for cheaper, simpler work and background ranking or matching.
  • Medium is the default for everyday assistance.
  • High is intended for demanding questions and may cost more or take longer, depending on the chosen model.

The names describe how you intend to use the models; they are not a guarantee of quality or price. Configure them with ai.models.low, ai.models.medium and ai.models.high. Blank Low or High settings use Medium. When migrating an older configuration, ai.models.chat still supplies Medium if it is blank, and ai.models.fast similarly supplies Low.

Ask for facts or instructions

Open the assistant from the app bar. Ask a specific question, such as "How do I upload episodes?", "What anime do I have?" or "Why is this download paused?". The assistant can search these guides for instructions and check available Arrk services for current information.

Follow-up questions can refer to recent results. Closing the popup clears the conversation. A persona changes the assistant's tone, not your permissions or the information available to it.

These guides are also readable without AI. Your administrator may have different features enabled from those described here.

Search before acting

Give the title and year, artist or season when names could be confused. Requests, watchlists and playback depend on the services available to your account. Adding a bookmark does not download a title, and an approved request does not mean it is ready to play.

Review any proposed action and its result. Deleting media and changing quality require an administrator and an explicit confirmation in Arrk. The assistant cannot bypass request approval or your account's limits.

Ranking, matching and privacy

AI can help choose between suitable music downloads or possible matches for uploaded videos. Normal matching and file checks still apply. If AI is unavailable or uncertain, Arrk keeps its usual non-AI choice. You still review upload matches before import.

For release ranking or import matching, shadow records what AI would choose without changing the result. ambiguous uses AI only for close choices; always considers it for eligible choices; off disables it. These settings are under ai.features.releaseRanking and ai.features.importMatching.

AI providers may charge for tokens, the pieces of text sent and received. Automatic features can incur costs without a chat message. Review calls, tokens and limits on AI Usage. Cost estimates require prices configured under ai.pricing; check your provider's billing for actual charges.

Prompt and response storage is off by default with ai.privacy.storePromptText: false; usage counts are still recorded. Turning local prompt storage off does not stop the provider receiving data needed for AI requests. Avoid sending passwords, keys or unnecessary personal details. Check the provider's own privacy policy.

Connect an external assistant with MCP

MCP, the Model Context Protocol, lets a compatible assistant app ask Arrk for information and permitted actions. The external app supplies its own AI service. Arrk's MCP connection does not require ai.enabled or an Arrk AI provider.

An administrator needs an approved, active Arrk account for the connection and an HTTPS address for Arrk. Use a separate non-administrator account unless administrative access is necessary. Open Users at /users, choose Edit user for that account and note the User ID shown beneath its username. MCP setup uses this number, not the username.

  1. Choose a client app that supports a remote MCP server using Streamable HTTP and a manually configured Authorization header.
  2. Generate a unique random secret of at least 32 characters. This is the connection's token: anyone holding it can act with the assigned account's allowed access. Do not reuse an AI provider key or an account password.
  3. In Configuration → AI, set ai.mcp.enabled to true. Add an entry to ai.mcp.clients with name, the account's userId, the secret as token, and allowWrites: false.
  4. In the client app, add Arrk's public HTTPS address followed by /mcp. Select Streamable HTTP if a transport choice is offered.
  5. Configure the header name Authorization and value Bearer <token>, replacing <token> with your secret. Keep it in the client's secure credential settings, not in the server URL.
  6. Connect and try a read-only task, such as searching the product guides. Verify the result before allowing changes.

Read-only is the default. Set that client's allowWrites to true only if you want actions such as requests or watchlist changes. The account's normal permissions still apply. Deletion and quality changes are not available through MCP; use Arrk for those.

Use a different token for each client. Replace or remove its configured token to revoke access. Disabled, deleted or pending accounts cannot connect. Signing into Arrk in a browser does not authenticate an MCP client, and clients that require automatic OAuth sign-in instead of a bearer header are not supported by this setup.

If connection fails, check that MCP is enabled, HTTPS reaches Arrk, the account is active and approved, and the client sends the exact token in the header. An unsupported client authentication method will not be fixed by entering the token as a URL parameter. Do not send tokens in screenshots or support messages.

When the assistant cannot help

AI can be unavailable because it is disabled, a provider failed or a usage limit was reached. Administrators can inspect AI Usage and the relevant error. A provider rate limit may trigger a retry using a different configured Low model; it is not a guarantee that the question will complete.

Normal browsing, playback, requests and these guides remain available without a model. Features such as ranking and upload matching keep their non-AI fallback. The assistant itself needs a working provider to answer chat questions.

Downloads, indexers and VPN

  • Indexers and sources
  • Read the Downloads page
  • Slow, stalled and errored torrents
  • Seeding and disk pressure
  • Route a service through VPN

Set up download sources, understand transfer states and recover safely from slow downloads or a full disk.

Indexers and sources

An indexer is a searchable catalogue of download releases. Arrk uses Prowlarr to connect torrent indexers to your library services. Transmission downloads torrents, while slskd downloads music from the Soulseek file-sharing network.

  1. As an administrator, add the indexer's settings in Configuration under indexers.entries, or use Prowlarr's own interface when its proxy is enabled.
  2. Use the correct indexer definition and credentials for your account. Requirements differ by provider; placeholder settings will not work.
  3. Test a known search before adding more sources.

Use only sources and content you are authorised to access. Keep indexer credentials private. The challenge solver under indexers.solver can help with supported website challenges, but cannot fix incorrect credentials or a provider outage. Disable administrative proxies you no longer need.

Read the Downloads page

Open Downloads at /downloads to see torrents and Soulseek transfers together. Cards show progress, speed, size and estimated time remaining. Torrents also show connected peers and a ratio, the amount uploaded compared with the amount downloaded.

  • Downloading means data is transferring; Queued means it is waiting.
  • Paused needs attention before it can continue.
  • Seeding means a completed torrent is sharing data with other people.
  • Error needs investigation; download completion alone does not mean a file has reached the library.

Administrators can pause, resume and cancel transfers, including bulk pause/resume. Cancelling manually does not automatically start a replacement search. Soulseek does not use torrent seeding or torrent cleanup rules. Transmission remains part of the stack; services.torrentDownloader.enabled is not a working disable switch.

Slow, stalled and errored torrents

A stalled torrent has stopped transferring with no peers or seeds available. A slow torrent is below the configured speed threshold. Arrk can remove persistently slow or stalled downloads and try another release. It holds those penalties while the measured internet connection is unhealthy, rather than treating an outage as every torrent's fault.

  1. Check the transfer's error, progress and peer count on Downloads.
  2. Check whether other transfers or the internet connection are also affected.
  3. Review Events for cleanup or retry activity before starting another search yourself.
  4. If an administrator revokes a penalty, check that the cause has improved first.

Error cleanup uses its own waiting period. Even a completed torrent can be removed after a persistent tracker error. Cleanup can delete downloaded files, so review settings under services.torrentDownloader.management before changing them.

A failed download can cause a different release to be tried. It does not permanently ban the movie, show or album from household requests.

Seeding and disk pressure

Seeding shares a completed torrent back to others. Choose goals that follow your tracker's rules. Under services.torrentDownloader.seeding, minimum seed time delays cleanup; ratio or maximum time can then cause a completed torrent to be removed.

By default, storage management starts removing seeding torrents when the downloads filesystem reaches 85% used. At 90%, it pauses torrents instead and skips that cleanup pass. Paused torrents do not automatically resume when space becomes available.

If storage fills up, free space safely, check Downloads and resume intentionally. Deleting an old download job and deleting a library title are different operations. Storage cleanup does not start replacement searches. Check which filesystem is full before removing library media.

Route a service through VPN

A VPN sends a service's traffic through a provider's encrypted connection. Arrk uses Gluetun to manage that connection. You need a supported VPN provider and the provider's connection details before enabling routing.

  1. In Configuration, enter your provider and connection type under VPN, with the required credentials or WireGuard details.
  2. Enable VPN routing for the service you want to protect. For Transmission, the setting is services.torrentDownloader.vpn.
  3. Save and check the VPN and downloader's health, then test a transfer you are authorised to download.
  4. Enable vpn.portForwarding only if your provider supports it and your setup needs it.

Routing is per service. Routing the downloader does not route your players or the whole stack. A service's VPN setting can start the tunnel even with vpn.enabled: false; switching off that global setting alone is not enough to remove every service's VPN routing.

If downloads stop after a change, check provider credentials, tunnel health and connectivity before changing indexers. Keep WireGuard private keys and other secrets out of support messages. A VPN does not replace access control or permission to download content.

Accounts, requests and remote access

  • Accounts and roles
  • Request a title
  • Request blacklist versus release failure
  • Remote access and HTTPS
  • Share a diagnostic safely

Invite your household, request titles and reach Arrk safely away from home.

Accounts and roles

Administrators manage accounts on Users at /users. A regular user can browse and request media; administrator-only actions include managing accounts and settings. Give that access only to people who need it.

  1. Replace the initial administrator password before inviting anyone.
  2. In Configuration, choose how new accounts are admitted with auth.registrationMode.
  3. Use Approval to review new accounts before they can sign in, or AdminOnly to keep account creation with administrators. Open allows open registration.
  4. Check the account's role before sharing access.

In My account at /account, users can manage their own account and link supported Discord or MyAnimeList identities when enabled. Password sign-in, external sign-in and creating accounts are separate settings.

Arrk can also provision accounts for players. Single sign-on, using Arrk to sign into another service, depends on the player and client supporting it. It is separate from allowing password sign-in to Arrk itself.

Request a title

Requests let a household user ask for media without adding it directly. Requests must be enabled, and the chosen kind of request must be allowed by the administrator.

  1. Find the movie, show, album or artist in discovery and open its details.
  2. Check the title, year or artist, then choose the available request action.
  3. Choose the offered scope and quality. A scope is how much you want, such as a series, season or episode.
  4. Open Requests at /requests to follow the decision. Owners can revoke their own pending requests; administrators can approve, deny or blacklist them.

Pending means waiting for moderation. Approved means the media service accepted the request, not that the download is complete. Check library availability before expecting playback. Failed and Denied are different: one reports an unsuccessful approval attempt, the other an administrator's decision.

Administrators can enable automatic approval for selected users or roles. requests.maxOpenPerUser limits pending requests; zero means unlimited. Existing series can currently prevent requests for another season or episode, even when those files are missing. Ask an administrator to manage the missing content instead.

Request blacklist versus release failure

A request blacklist prevents future requests for a title in that media category. It is different from avoiding one broken download release. A successful download elsewhere does not remove the request blacklist.

Administrators should use Blacklist deliberately. With requests.blacklistOnDeny enabled, denying a request also blacklists it. There is currently no general un-blacklist control, so denial without blacklisting is the less permanent choice when appropriate.

A failed torrent or music source may be avoided while another download is tried. That does not mean the title has been banned from requests.

Remote access and HTTPS

Remote access needs a reachable address and a secure connection. HTTPS encrypts traffic between the browser and your server. A reverse proxy accepts that traffic and sends it to the right service; Arrk uses Traefik for its routes.

  1. Arrange HTTPS through your proxy or a configured tunnel before exposing account sign-in publicly.
  2. Set routes.publicUrl to the exact public address. Arrk uses it for shared links and player sign-in redirects.
  3. Enable only the service routes you intend to expose. When proxied, Jellyfin and Navidrome use /jellyfin and /navidrome.
  4. Enable auth.requireHttps when Arrk is reachable only through HTTPS.
  5. Test sign-in, a shared link and player access from outside your home network.

A Cloudflare tunnel can provide access without opening host ports; it needs its secret token under routes.cloudflared. Tunnel-only installations can set routes.httpPort and routes.httpsPort to zero. Keep a safe administrative access route while changing connectivity.

Setting an HTTPS public address does not automatically obtain a certificate. Certificate automation is not complete; your proxy or tunnel must provide working HTTPS. A hard-to-guess address is not a substitute for account security.

Share a diagnostic safely

When asking for help, include the failed action, approximate time, affected title, your account role and the visible error. Check Events at /events for related activity.

Remove passwords, API keys, cookies, tunnel tokens and webhook URLs before sharing logs or screenshots. Signed playback URLs can grant access to a video too. Share a short relevant error, not an entire configuration file.

Watchlists, history, pins and storage cleanup

  • Watchlist is not a download
  • History and the staleness clock
  • Thresholds and protections
  • Review before enabling deletion
  • Download cleanup is separate

Save titles for later, review what you have watched and protect favourites before cleaning up space.

Watchlist is not a download

Use watchlists on Movies or TV to organise titles you want to remember. Adding a title bookmarks it; it does not request or download it. Removing a bookmark does not delete its video file.

  1. Open a movie or series and use its watchlist action.
  2. Find saved titles in the Watchlists shelf on /movies or /tv.
  3. Create or manage named watchlists from that shelf as needed.

Some lists come from an external service and are read-only. Change those at their source. A bookmark gives a library title a longer cleanup grace period, not permanent protection. Ask an administrator to pin media that should never be considered stale.

History and the staleness clock

Open History at /history to review your playback. Administrators can select a user and filter or search the timeline. Arrk records playback through its own players and Jellyfin clients. External Navidrome-client listening is not attributed to an individual Arrk account in that history.

Stale means a downloaded title has gone unused for the configured time. New items age from when they were added; watching or listening resets the relevant clock. Playing an episode also refreshes its season, and playing a track refreshes its album.

For TV, cleanup considers downloaded seasons, not just individual episodes. Movies and music albums are considered individually. Unwatched media can become stale too; never assume it is protected merely because nobody has started it.

Thresholds and protections

The defaults mark media stale after 30 days and allow 45 days for bookmarked video or music kept in playlists. Early warnings and automatic deletion are off by default.

  • Watchlists and playlists extend the grace period; they do not protect forever.
  • An administrator pin excludes an item from stale warnings and automatic cleanup.
  • Pinning a series protects its seasons and episodes. A broader pin also protects the items beneath it.

Administrators can review the settings in Configuration under monitoring.tv.stale and monitoring.music.stale. upperThreshold sets days until stale; keepThreshold sets the longer grace period. lowerThreshold and keepLowerThreshold control early warnings, with zero disabling those warnings. autoCleanup permits automatic deletion for that library.

Review before enabling deletion

Only administrators can manage cleanup at /stale. Before turning on automatic deletion, review what Arrk considers old and check that playback history reflects how your household actually watches or listens.

  1. Open Stale and review the stale, about-to-be-stale and pinned tabs.
  2. Check each title's remaining time and estimated space.
  3. Pin favourites and anything you cannot replace.
  4. Back up files you need to preserve before using one-off or bulk delete actions.
  5. Observe the results over time before enabling autoCleanup for either library.

Automatic cleanup deletes only when explicitly enabled for that library. Watching or listening again resets age, and pins remain protected. Review season-level scope carefully before deleting TV content.

Download cleanup is separate

Download cleanup removes old or unhealthy transfers according to seeding, speed and storage rules. Media cleanup removes library content according to age, playback and pins. Changing one policy does not change the other.

If space is low, first check whether the full disk holds downloads or library files. A paused download may need space freed and a manual resume; pinning a film does not solve a full download disk. For any proposed library deletion, check the exact titles and scope before confirming.

Music discovery, acquisition and listening

  • Library and discovery
  • Add music and follow acquisition
  • Import checks and failed sources
  • Playback, previews and playlists
  • Lyrics and missing tracks

Find albums and artists, follow downloads and tell a short preview from a song in your library.

Library and discovery

Music discovery uses Deezer for artist, album and track information. Arrk organises your music library, and Navidrome serves its audio for playback. A discovery result is not necessarily downloaded.

Open an album or artist to see its details and available actions. Album availability is based on its tracks: Partial means only some tracks are present. Adding an artist does not immediately download every album.

Only acquire music you are authorised to access. Before expecting a download, an administrator must configure a working source: torrents, Soulseek, or both. Soulseek is a file-sharing network accessed through the slskd service.

Add music and follow acquisition

  1. Find the artist or album in music discovery and open its details.
  2. Check the artist and edition so you do not add a similarly named release.
  3. Use the available add action, or request the item if your account needs approval.
  4. For an album download, follow progress on Downloads and in the album's track list.
  5. Wait for import to complete before playing the full album.

Album acquisition runs in the background. Arrk normally tries torrents first, then Soulseek; individual tracks generally use Soulseek. Administrators choose the sources with services.music.useTorrents and services.music.useSoulseek.

Music requests offer Best Available, Lossless and Lossy. Lossless preserves the encoded audio without further loss; lossy uses compression that discards some audio information. Adding or approving an artist request records the artist but does not immediately download its albums.

If Soulseek is unavailable, pending acquisition can wait until it recovers. Repeated failures can eventually leave an item waiting for an explicit retry. Check progress and Events rather than repeatedly submitting the same request.

Import checks and failed sources

After downloading, Arrk checks that the files match the intended music before adding them to the library. A completed transfer may therefore still fail import. Files with the wrong album or an implausible track length are not accepted just because their names look similar.

Arrk excludes releases marked as mono, meaning single-channel recordings, from normal acquisition. An artist actually named Mono is not excluded. If a particular edition cannot be found, check whether that restriction applies.

A failed download source can be avoided temporarily while another is tried. That is different from permanently blocking a household request. AI ranking, when enabled, helps choose between suitable downloads; it does not remove file checks.

Playback, previews and playlists

A Deezer preview is a short sample you explicitly play, not the full local song. Preview tracks do not enter album or playlist playback queues. Normal queued listening uses tracks already available in your library.

Open the album or playlist and use its playback actions. If tracks are missing from the queue, compare their availability with the downloaded tracks rather than assuming the player skipped files it has.

Playlists you own in Navidrome can be edited. External Deezer playlist subscriptions are read-only; change the source playlist rather than expecting to edit its contents in Arrk. Listening through Arrk records personal history. Listening in an external Navidrome client is not attributed to your individual Arrk account in that history.

Lyrics and missing tracks

Lyrics come from a separate service and may not exist for every track or match every recording perfectly. A missing lyric does not mean the audio download failed. A genuine no-result is not retried repeatedly in the background; temporary service failures are treated differently.

For missing audio, check these in order.

  1. Confirm it is a library track, not only a discovery result or preview.
  2. Check whether the album was actually added or requested for download.
  3. Look for an active or failed transfer on Downloads.
  4. Check Events for a match or import error.
  5. If the file imported but will not play, check Navidrome's health and library visibility.

Avoid moving or renaming library files as the first fix. Keep the relevant error and title details so an administrator can investigate without losing the original evidence.

Events, notifications and Discord

  • Events versus inbox
  • Choose topics and delivery
  • Follow a title
  • Enable Discord direct messages
  • Missing or noisy alerts

Find recent activity, follow titles and choose which alerts reach you or a shared channel.

Events versus inbox

Open the app-bar bell for live activity and unread notifications. Dismiss an item or use Mark all read to clear unread alerts. Open Events at /events for the wider activity history, with categories and search. Downloads shows activity relevant to transfers.

Events record what happened. Notifications are the alerts you choose to receive about some of those events. Turning off a notification does not erase the underlying event. Not every event has an alert, so use Events when investigating a missing message.

Choose topics and delivery

A topic is a category such as downloads, requests or system health. Choose the topics you want in notification settings. Administrators can also configure shared Discord or webhook delivery. A webhook sends messages to a configured destination, such as a Discord channel or an automation service.

Start with a small set of useful alerts, then adjust after seeing the volume. Shared delivery settings do not mean every personal alert goes to a public channel. Retention limits how long inbox entries are kept; notifications are not a backup of your library or configuration.

For manual configuration, notifications.topics controls enabled categories. Discord and generic webhook settings can route categories to different destinations. A channel's exclude setting suppresses its delivery without removing the in-app alert. Leave notifications.showJobActivity off unless you need background-task messages for troubleshooting.

Follow a title

Requesting a title follows it automatically. A series or season follow includes its episodes. Adding a title to a watchlist also follows it, so you can receive relevant updates without watching the Downloads page continuously.

Removing the last bookmark removes that watchlist's follow, but a separate manual or request follow can remain. Request decisions can still notify you after unfollowing because they answer your request; the follow's status preference controls those alerts.

Personal alerts go to the interested accounts and their direct delivery channels, not the global webhook. Expect important changes and problems rather than a direct message for every download percentage update.

Enable Discord direct messages

You need a linked Discord account, a configured bot and a server shared with that bot. Your Discord privacy settings must allow messages from server members.

  1. An administrator creates or chooses a Discord application and obtains its bot token from the Discord developer portal.
  2. The administrator configures the bot under notifications.discord.directMessages and invites it to a server the intended users belong to.
  3. Each user opens My account in Arrk and links Discord.
  4. Open Events and use the Discord row to check the direct-message toggle and send a test.
  5. If the test fails, check the shared server and Discord message permissions before trying again.

Unlinking Discord or turning direct messages off stops delivery. A Discord webhook for a shared channel is a different setup from the bot used for personal messages. Keep both webhook URLs and bot tokens private.

Missing or noisy alerts

  1. Look in Events for the original action and its time.
  2. Check whether the topic is enabled and, for a title update, whether you follow it with the relevant categories enabled.
  3. Check the intended destination: personal messages do not automatically go to the shared channel.
  4. For Discord direct messages, use the test action and review its result.
  5. Ask an administrator to check delivery settings, routing and exclusions if the in-app alert exists but the external message does not.

For noise, turn off categories you do not need or suppress a channel rather than losing all useful alerts. If an expected event is absent too, the action may have failed or may not yet produce that alert. Share the relevant error with private destination details removed.

Video playback and subtitles

  • Play and resume
  • Audio and subtitle selection
  • Get missing subtitles
  • Stream or transcode problems

Watch an imported title, choose audio and subtitles, and work through common playback problems.

Play and resume

Before playing, the title needs a video file in the library and must be visible to Jellyfin, Arrk's video player service. A discovery result or approved request is not enough.

  1. Open the movie or episode and choose Play.
  2. Use Continue Watching to return to an unfinished video or the next episode of a series.
  3. Choose audio and subtitles from the player's track menus if needed.

Continue Watching is personal to your account and shows one card per series. Near-end viewing can count as finished, so the next episode may appear even if you did not watch every credit.

Near the end of an episode, autoplay shows a next-episode card. Play now advances immediately. Dismissing the card, seeking back or pressing Escape cancels the countdown.

Administrators can use services.jellyfin.webPlayer.enabled to choose between Arrk's in-site player and Jellyfin's own web client. Turning it off does not remove Jellyfin or the library.

Audio and subtitle selection

Open the player's track menus to choose an available language or subtitle track. Changing audio may briefly restart the stream at your current position.

Text subtitles can usually switch quickly. Image-based subtitles, such as PGS from a disc, may need to be burned into the video. That means the server draws them into each frame and can require more processing power. Different subtitle tracks can therefore have noticeably different performance.

Use the subtitle appearance menu for text size, background opacity, outline and style. Those preferences are saved in your browser. Opening title details from the player pauses playback; it resumes afterwards only if it was playing before.

Get missing subtitles

An administrator must enable subtitles and configure at least one provider, the service supplying subtitle files. The built-in OpenSubtitles provider requires your API key. Bazarr is another, optional service for additional providers; it is not required for OpenSubtitles.

  1. In Configuration, enable subtitles and choose languages under services.subtitles.
  2. For OpenSubtitles, enter services.subtitles.opensubtitles.apiKey; add account credentials if you want to use the account's quota.
  3. Review automatic download and score settings. A minimum score filters weaker matches; it does not guarantee perfect timing.
  4. For older library items, use Get missing or a manual subtitle search from the item's available subtitle controls.

When automatic download is enabled, new imports are checked for missing languages. Existing subtitles inside the video can already satisfy language coverage. Separate subtitle files stored beside the video also count. If no provider is configured, subtitle controls may be hidden.

Provider download quotas still apply. Repeated attempts do not reset them. If using Bazarr, leave its independent wanted search out of the way so it does not compete with Arrk's automatic searches.

Stream or transcode problems

Transcoding means converting video or audio while it plays so your browser can handle it. Jellyfin performs that work. A file can play smoothly with one audio/subtitle choice but require conversion with another.

  1. Check that Jellyfin is healthy and the title is present in its library.
  2. Try another available audio track or text subtitles instead of image subtitles.
  3. Try another supported browser to narrow down a compatibility issue.
  4. Check the server's available CPU or GPU capacity and relevant errors in Events or logs.

NVIDIA acceleration requires a compatible GPU and working host support. Administrators can enable it with services.jellyfin.nvidia; turning the setting on cannot supply missing hardware or drivers.

For support, describe the browser, title, selected tracks and error. Do not share signed playback URLs or player access tokens; they can grant access to media.

Installation, storage and configuration

  • First start
  • Storage and backups
  • Editing configuration
  • Upgrades and legacy installations
  • When setup fails

Start Arrk safely, choose where files live and preserve your settings when upgrading.

First start

Arrk runs and configures the services behind your media library. You need a Linux host with Docker, internet access and space for configuration, downloads and media. Docker runs each service in a container, a separate application environment on the same host.

Arrk needs access to the Docker socket to manage those containers. That access gives it extensive control over the host. Install it only on a machine you control.

  1. Choose persistent directories for configuration, downloads and media before installation.
  2. From the repository, use ./scripts/run-arrk.sh, or use docker compose up -d for the included Compose deployment.
  3. Open Arrk on your host's port 5186, unless you changed the port.
  4. On a fresh installation, sign in with admin / admin and change the password immediately in My account.
  5. Keep the installation private while you configure access and test the library.

The published image is ghcr.io/dynamiquel/arrk:latest. The launcher uses ./arrk-data by default and reuses ./stackarr-data when it exists. Compose retains its legacy storage default so upgrades do not silently start with empty directories.

Storage and backups

Keep the directories mounted at /config, /downloads and /media persistent. Configuration includes accounts, settings and keys; media holds your library; downloads holds temporary and completed transfers awaiting import.

Back up configuration and any separate Docker configuration volumes used by managed services. A volume is storage Docker maintains outside a container's disposable files. Saving only the Arrk configuration file does not back up the whole stack. Include media in your backup plan if you need to recover the files themselves.

Leave enough free space for a download and its imported copy. Uploaded videos are copied into the library, so staging and the finished file can occupy space at the same time.

The default TV root is $media/tv, with movies and shows beneath it; music uses $media/music. Administrators can change these through storage.tv and storage.music. Moving a configured root does not move an existing library automatically. Back up first, update mounts and settings, then check the library folders in the affected service.

Editing configuration

Open Configuration for validated editing, help text and version history. Most changes are picked up without restarting Arrk, though a managed service may take time to apply them. Change one area at a time and check the result before continuing.

Administrators who prefer manual editing can use /config/arrk.yaml. The configuration editor's schema lists supported options. Keep an external backup even when version history is available, and remove secrets before sharing an example.

For full movie and TV discovery, add a TMDb API key or read token under Metadata. TMDb supplies titles, artwork and descriptions. The manual settings are metadata.tmdbApiKey and metadata.tmdbReadToken. Without them, discovery is limited but library-manager search remains available. Music metadata does not need a Deezer API key.

Upgrades and legacy installations

Keep your existing configuration and storage rather than creating new empty directories during an upgrade.

  1. Back up configuration, service configuration volumes and any library files you cannot replace.
  2. Stop the old Arrk application before starting its replacement.
  3. Pull the new image and recreate the container with the same configuration directory mounted at /config, the same media/download mounts and the same StackName.
  4. Sign in and check your accounts, settings, library and playback before deleting any backup.

Do not rename or delete legacy stackarr.yaml, stackarr.json or stackarr.db files. Keep any accompanying database files together too. Arrk reads existing installations in place; old configuration filenames take precedence when both old and new names exist. Fresh installations use arrk.yaml and arrk.db.

Never run old and new versions against the same configuration at once. Existing Docker resources may still have stackarr in their names; that is expected and is not a reason to rename or remove them.

When setup fails

Check that Docker is available, storage mounts point to the intended directories, the disk has free space and no other application is using the chosen host ports. Multiple Arrk installations need different StackName values and non-overlapping host ports.

If Arrk opens, check Events at /events and application logs at /logs for the failing service. If it does not open, use docker logs -f arrk for an installation whose container is named arrk. Share only the relevant error with credentials removed, not your entire configuration.

Movies, TV, anime and local uploads

  • Discovery versus library
  • Add, request and search
  • Quality profiles
  • Upload a known title
  • Auto-detect and correct a match
  • Finished downloading but not playable

Find something to watch, request missing titles and add video files you already own.

Discovery versus library

Open Discover to browse movies, shows and seasonal anime. Discovery is a catalogue of titles you might want; seeing a title there does not mean you have its video file. Movies at /movies and TV at /tv show your library.

Full discovery needs TMDb credentials configured by an administrator. TMDb supplies movie and TV information and artwork. Without those credentials, search through the library services still works, but discovery and anime results are limited.

Read the title's state before choosing what to do next.

  • Downloaded means a movie has a file, or a series has every aired episode.
  • Downloaded Monitored means every episode in the seasons selected for monitoring is present.
  • Partial means some files are present; Missing means none are present.
  • Downloading means a matching transfer is in progress, not that it is ready to watch.

Monitoring means asking the library service to look for missing or improved files. Specials are not counted in normal season progress.

Add, request and search

  1. Search or browse Discover and open the title's details.
  2. Check the title, year and, for TV, season or episode scope.
  3. As an administrator, use Add to Library and choose the available quality and search options. Other users can request the title for approval.
  4. Follow the request on Requests or the transfer on Downloads. Wait for import before expecting playback.

An interactive search lets you inspect individual releases, the downloadable versions of a title. Rejected releases are hidden by default; read rejection reasons before overriding a choice.

For a library using only local files, an administrator can set services.tv.search.enabled: false. This hides search and retry actions but keeps upload available. It does not make your existing library disappear.

Quality profiles

A quality profile sets the resolutions Arrk will accept and whether it should upgrade later. Choose the profile when adding or requesting a title. The defaults include Best Available, FHD for 1080p and UHD for 2160p.

Higher resolution is not always better: bitrate, the amount of video data per second, also matters. Default minimum bitrate settings are 3 Mbps for 1080p and 12 Mbps for 2160p. These affect future downloads, not removal of existing files. Upgrades use extra download traffic and storage.

Administrators manage profiles in Configuration under qualityProfiles.profiles and bitrate floors under qualityProfiles.minimumBitratesMbps. Setting a bitrate tier to zero leaves it unmanaged. Back up before changing the profile list: profiles removed from it can be removed from the library services too. Changes to an existing profile may not update that profile in those services; check there if the results do not match your settings.

Upload a known title

You need an administrator account, a supported video file and enough free space for a temporary copy and the imported file. An import adds a file to the organised library; it is separate from uploading the bytes.

  1. Open the matching title in Discover and choose Upload beside Add to Library, or open the title already in your library.
  2. In the library, movie details offer Upload; series details offer Upload episodes; an episode menu offers Upload file.
  3. Choose the video files and any separate subtitle files in the same batch.
  4. Review the target and episode mapping, then confirm the import.
  5. Wait for the imported file to appear in the library and player.

Arrk copies uploads into their final library folders. Successful temporary copies are normally deleted afterwards; failed copies can remain for retry until the configured retention period expires. Administrators can adjust limits under services.tv.uploads if needed.

Auto-detect and correct a match

Use auto-detect upload on a library page when you do not want to select a title first. Arrk suggests a match and shows a score, alternatives and season/episode mapping. The score is a hint, not proof that the match is right.

  1. Check the title and year, especially for remakes with the same name.
  2. Review every episode mapping, particularly for anime using continuous episode numbers.
  3. Choose another candidate or use manual TMDb search if the suggestion is wrong.
  4. Enable the replace switch only if you intend to overwrite an existing file.
  5. Confirm when the target is correct. Nothing imports before confirmation.

AI matching can help choose between suggestions when enabled, but your review still matters. Separate subtitle files are matched to the imported video and become available after the player library refreshes.

Finished downloading but not playable

A completed transfer still needs to be imported and then discovered by Jellyfin, the video player service.

  1. Check Downloads for completion or an error.
  2. Check Events for import activity and any rejection or file-access problem.
  3. Confirm the library title actually has a file, not just an entry.
  4. Allow time for Jellyfin to refresh, then try playback again.

If import fails, check disk space, folder permissions and the file's match before downloading another copy. Administrators can inspect the underlying library service for more detailed import errors.
